posts.title: A Connecticut Yankee Counterfactual at Auschwitz: On Elon Musk's Holocaust "What Ifs"
posts.description: I was happy to contribute some thoughts to Shira Li Bartov's new article in The Forward, "Could Social Media Really Have Stopped the Holocaust?" which addresses Elon Musk's use of counterfactuals to reflect on the legacy of the Holocaust. See article LINK Here are my full comments, some of which appear verbatim in the article, which also quotes leading Holocaust scholars and Jewish historians like Christopher Browning, Doris Bergen, and David Myers. When Musk visited Auschwitz the other day, he was reported as saying that " [if] there [had] been social media at the time of World War II, the Holocaust 'would have been impossible to hide' and lives could have been saved." As I noted: Musk’s comments are the latest examples of how people often use counterfactual claims about the past to justify various agendas in the present. posts.title: It's Finally Out! PREDICTING THE PAST is Now Available
posts.description: I began writing this blog thirteen years ago in 2013. In my first post, I wrote of my eagerness to " better understand why we are increasingly wondering 'what if?' by examining how "[counterfactual] observations about the past" were "becom[ing]...commonplace in our present-day world." More than a decade later, I am presenting my conclusions. Predicting the Past is nearly 900 pages long and covers 3000 years of western history. (It was originally 600 manuscript pages longer, egads). I've revised it at least half a dozen times. In its final form, it represents the distillation of my thinking on the topic. Could it have been shorter? Of course. But it's futile to wonder what might have been. (LOL. At least that's what some of the skeptics I discuss in the book would have said, if they were able to see it today). posts.title: What if the American Revolution Had Failed? (Updated to include Curtis Yarvin's 2008 counterfactual fantasy)
posts.description: To mark the US semiquincentennial, I wrote this new piece discussing how Americans have wondered "what if" about the American Revolution. Thanks to the folks at Real Clear History for publishing it. I'm pasting it below and have added a paragraph that cites Curtis Yarvin's rightwing fantasy from 2008 about the revolution failing and leaving the US under (superior) monarchical rule. I had kept the reference in a file I had forgotten about and only just stumbled upon, which is why I neglected to include it in my original piece. Oh well. Here it is included below (highlighted in yellow ) What If the American Revolution Had Failed? As the United States marks the 250th anniversary of the nation’s founding, many Americans are reflecting on the revolution’s legacy by visiting historical exhibitions, attending regional fairs, and watching battle reenactments.
